text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"Los Angeles, CA","level":"city","category":"rent_increase_limits","status":"in_force","title":"Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) allowable annual rent increase","requirement":"Rent on covered units may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage published by LAHD. Effective February 2, 2026, landlords can no longer add a percentage for utilities, and the additional 10% for an added dependent is no longer permitted. A 10% increase is still allowed for an additional non-dependent tenant, within 60 days of the landlord learning of that tenant. Rent may be raised to market rate when the tenant voluntarily moves out, is evicted for nonpayment or lease violation, is evicted for failure to comply with a Tenant Habitability Plan or per a City Attorney order, or accepts a Tenant Buyout Agreement. Additional increases requiring LAHD approval are available through the Capital Improvement, Primary Renovation, Seismic Retrofit and Rehabilitation programs and the Just and Reasonable Rent Increase. At-fault reasons: failure to fix or address a violation of the rental agreement, and creating a nuisance or causing damage to the unit. No-fault reasons: the owner or an immediate family member moving in, a resident manager moving in, demolition and permanent removal from the rental market, and a government order. No-fault evictions require payment of tenant relocation assistance. For no-fault evictions the landlord must file a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD and give the tenant a 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require a 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension). All termination notices for RSO units must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service on the tenant.
